intro: Our thoughts and ramblings on doughnuts and other things.

posts.title: Avoiding the line at Britt's Donuts

image.alt: Britt's Donut Shop at Carolina Beach, surprisingly empty on a rainy day

body: We have been trying to get to Britt’s Donuts for years. 5 years to be exact. In April when they were getting ready to open for the season, I excitedly told my hairdresser that this was the year we were finally going to go. She told me they had permanently closed down and then proceeded to cut my bangs too short.

I really appreciate how many people write in to share their donut news, but there’s a reason we fact check things. One of the owners of Britt’s did pass away earlier this year, but the shop still opened this season. My heart can take having too-short bangs, but missing out on Britt’s would have literally killed me.

I have heard how long the lines are at Britt’s and how long people spend waiting. As someone in their thirties or forties, it’s only a matter of time before some younger, hotter donut enthusiast replaces me. I simply can’t afford to wait. So the only remaining option was to go at open.

The drive from Raleigh to Wilmington is about 2 hours. We woke up at 5am to try to leave at 5:30, but left at 6am because even though I don’t have time to wait in a line, I do have time to complain about getting up at 5 in the morning to try to avoid waiting in line. Rainstorms moved through the state, which means our usual summer hellfires were temporarily replaced by slightly milder and damper summer hellfires.

Right around 8am on a rainy Saturday morning, there’s hardly anyone at the Carolina Beach Boardwalk. At the shop there were less than a handful of people in line and plenty of open seating. Britt’s only makes one type of donut: glazed. I love when I don’t have to think about my order. We got a half dozen and a small coffee, which came out at record speed. If they had a gumball machine, it probably would have taken longer for the gumball to drop. They do not have a gumball machine.

Sitting at the counter, you can see the donuts getting fried in what looks like a vessel from the 1930s: industrial, sturdy, and possibly haunted. It’s an impressive and seemingly long-lasting piece of tech that makes the outside of the donuts just a little bit crispy and keeps the inside nice and soft. I think so many people like this place because it feels so unchanged. They’re cash-only, so in a day and age where you can use your phone or retina scan to pay, it’s a nice change of pace. I assume the feeling is different when there’s a line out the door, the floor is wet with seawater, and someone’s sunburned uncle is yelling their order to the teenagers at the counter, but the whole thing felt like a slower, gentler experience. You pay with cash, sit at the counter, get your order and enjoy at your leisure.

Ultimately, this is a lovely donut experience if you’re able to avoid a line or can afford to hire someone to stand in line for you. And while I have no scientific backing for this, I think not having to wait makes a donut taste sweeter.

posts.title: The 2026 Raleigh Donut Maps are Live
body: Somewhere in 2021 or 2022 I created the Raleigh and Washington DC Donut maps. I posted what I had created on Reddit and one of the first comments I got was that I shouldn’t have wasted my time and made a fried chicken map instead.
What a time to be alive.

Here we are 5 or 6 or some amount of years later, in 2026, with a new, glorious set of [Raleigh Donut Maps](/Raleigh-Donut-Map/). The lack of fried chicken maps still make my heart weep, but we soldier on.

I started this project before AI was common. The amount of digging I did to find and share all of the local donut vendors we have in and around Raleigh is straight up bananas to me now. Hours and hours of work, interacting with folks online, and going out to test out new donut places. Fully worth it, we made a ton of friends, but keeping up with these ventures can be difficult. We dropped off for a bit, I don’t think I’ve updated instagram in at least a year, but we’re back.

For full transparency, this new website was built using Claude. The donut maps were not and our donut data isn’t either. A software engineer and a web accessibility analyst got together, had a baby, and apparently it ended up looking like the page you’re currently navigating. We worked from sketches in notebooks, tweaked everything to make it easier to navigate with a screen reader and keyboard, and generally tried to keep things clean and easy.

The [Raleigh Donut Maps](/Raleigh-Donut-Map/) are built out on Google Maps and also presented as a handy website list. The maps and list both have filters you can use and a handy search tool. We did our best to update the maps with any new locations. If there’s a spot we missed, you can mosey over to our contact form or email us at hello@doughnut-days.com.
It’s nice to be back online. I hope these maps make your life a little sweeter.
